newsitem.title: USA: Local bar associations should follow ABA lead--SEC.
newsitem.headline: Local bar associations should follow ABA lead--SEC.

text.p: SEC Chairman Arthur Levitt on Wednesday told lawyers at an American Bar Association convention that the group's vote to condemn "pay-to-play" set the stage for state and local bar associations to follow suit.
However, Levitt made it clear that further steps might be needed. "This is just a beginning as far as I'm concerned," he told reporters.
Later, when asked if the resolution went far enough, he replied, "There is no one single action that will eliminate all graft and corruption."
"I am very pleased," Levitt said, adding it would be difficult for local bar associations not to join the ABA's action.

In prepared remarks released shortly afterward, Levitt hammered this point home. "Tomorrow, we'll begin a national campaign against pay-to-play by working in every state to convince state and local bar associations to eliminate this odious practice."

Levitt saluted Michael Cordozo, who heads the Association of the Bar of the City of New York, Judge William Webster, the former FBI director, former Attorney General Elliot Richardson, and William Allen, the former Chancellor of Delaware's Court of Chancery.
All four serve on a committee formed by SEC to press for a ban on pay-to-play, the practice of giving political donations designed to win municipal bond business.
Cordozo told reporters at the convention, "It's now up to the local boards to be working on this."
The approximately 575 ABA delegates approved the resolution condemning pay-to-play in a voice vote.
